summary: Router 0.34.1 changes how the prompt rate is computed from the Ollama response statistics of a finished request: perf_stats reads the optional prompt_eval_cached_count and rates the processed tokens; Node.note_perf passes a prompt rate to the Home Assistant MQTT sensors only when that count is known and at least 200. Traced callers: perf_record (proxy.py end of request, ops.py shadow runs, bench) and admin.py try-it display; consumers of the result: the passive averages and samples in perf.json, Node.last_prompt -> ha.py snapshot -> MQTT sensor node_<n>_prompt_tps. The routing score (EWMA) uses gen_tps and ttft only, so routing, placement, authentication, the tunnel protocol, the cloud payload and the request/response bodies passed to clients are unchanged. The new input comes from the node's Ollama through the agent tunnel (B3), which could already report any rate; the value is type-checked (numbers only, booleans excluded), clamped to 0..prompt_eval_count like Ollama, and only changes a telemetry number. No new route, key, dependency, workflow or permission.

tests.evidence: ALLE OK, including cache hit, uncached, partly cached, missing, negative, oversized, string and boolean cached counts; the same test fails on the old code (KeyError prompt_new).
0 failures; passive performance data and benchmark checks pass with responses that carry no cached count.

limitations: Pre-existing, not changed here: perf_stats does not reject NaN or negative durations from a node; a node can report arbitrary rates, which only affect telemetry. With this change a NaN cached count is clamped and a NaN processed count never reaches Home Assistant.
Not tested against a live Ollama; the field semantics follow Ollama's PR 17943 (prompt_eval_count = whole prompt, prompt_eval_cached_count = cached part, duration = processed part).
